intro.title: What does Exyconn build for law firms and legal teams?
intro.definition: is software that takes the clerical and first-pass work of a law firm, such as screening enquiries, marking up contracts, finding past drafts, watching cause lists and recording time, so lawyers spend their hours on advice and advocacy. Exyconn designs, builds and runs these agents on your matter management system, document store, email and calendar. They draft and flag; a lawyer reviews and decides, and nothing is sent to a client unchecked.

benefits.title: Why firms are doing this now

items.text: Clients expect a marked-up contract in days, and much of a first review is checking clauses against positions the firm already holds.
A firm's best precedents sit in partners' folders and old email threads where nobody else can find them.
Hearing dates move with every cause list, and a missed limitation date cannot be undone.
Time recorded at month end from memory is time that is under-billed or written off.
Clients now ask in writing how their documents are protected, including from AI tools.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a firm's unbilled hours actually go
props.lede: Partners and associates name the same list. Very little of it is law; all of it has to be done carefully.

items.title: Enquiries that are not yet matters
items.text: Calls and messages arrive with half the facts. Someone senior has to read each one to decide whether it is in the firm's practice areas, urgent, or not a matter at all.

items.title: Conflict checks by email
items.text: A new client's name is circulated to the partners and checked against memory and an old spreadsheet. It works until the related company or the other side's director is missed.

items.title: Associates reading boilerplate
items.text: Every NDA, lease and vendor agreement gets a full read to find the five clauses that differ from the firm's standard position. The associate's time goes into finding them, not judging them.

items.title: Drafts the firm has already written
items.text: A good share-purchase agreement or written submission exists somewhere in the document store, but finding it means knowing who worked on it and what they named the file.

items.title: Cause lists checked by hand
items.text: Clerks check daily cause lists and case status across several courts and tribunals, then update a diary. Adjournments, new dates and limitation periods all depend on that one manual step.

items.title: Time reconstructed at month end
items.text: Calls, emails and drafting are pieced together from calendars and sent folders before invoices go out. What is forgotten is never billed, and narratives are too vague for clients to accept.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off your lawyers and clerks

items.title: Client intake and conflict checks
items.text: Answers enquiries that come to your website, email or WhatsApp, collects the facts and parties, checks names against your matter management system for conflicts and books a consultation. It does not give advice or go looking for clients.

items.title: First-pass contract review
items.text: Compares an incoming contract with your playbook clause by clause, marks deviations in tracked changes with the firm's fallback wording and lists missing clauses. The associate reviews every change before it goes to the client.

items.title: Research over your own precedents
items.text: Searches the firm's past drafts, opinions, pleadings and notes in your document store and returns the relevant passages with links to the source file. It only searches documents the lawyer asking is allowed to open.

items.title: Deadlines and hearing dates
items.text: Reads cause lists and case status for your matters each day, updates hearing dates in the matter system and calendars, and computes reply and limitation deadlines for a lawyer to confirm. Changes are sent to the matter team on email or WhatsApp.

items.title: Time tracking and billing
items.text: Suggests time entries from calls, meetings, emails and document edits against the right matter, for the lawyer to accept or change. Approved time flows into draft invoices with clear narratives for partner review.

items.title: Confidentiality and access control
items.text: Applies matter-level permissions and ethical walls to every agent action, so no one sees a document through the AI that they could not open directly. Every query and document view is logged for the partners.

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day at a twelve-lawyer litigation and corporate firm
props.lede: A Monday with two hearings and a closing on Friday. Each moment lights the part of the practice the agent is working on.

moments.title: The day's board, already read
moments.text: Today's cause lists are checked for the firm's matters. One case has moved from item 14 to item 3, and the junior on it gets a WhatsApp before leaving home.

moments.title: An overnight enquiry, sorted
moments.text: A startup founder wrote in at midnight about a co-founder exit. The agent has collected the shareholding, checked both names for conflicts and booked a call with the corporate partner.

moments.title: A vendor agreement marked up
moments.text: A client sends a 40-page master services agreement. In minutes the associate has a tracked-changes draft showing the indemnity, liability cap and termination clauses that differ from the firm's playbook.

moments.title: An ethical wall holds
moments.text: A trainee searches for a company name that belongs to a matter they are walled off from. The agent returns nothing from that matter, and the attempt is logged for the managing partner.

moments.title: Last year's submissions, found
moments.text: An associate asks for the firm's written submissions on interim injunctions in trademark cases. The agent returns three past filings with the relevant paragraphs and links to each file.

moments.title: The day's time, ready to approve
moments.text: Each lawyer gets suggested entries for the day's calls, emails and drafting, matched to matters. Most are accepted with one tap, and the narratives are ready for the month's invoices.

items.question: Does this replace associates or paralegals?
items.answer: No. It takes the first pass: finding deviations, pulling precedents, updating dates and drafting time entries. A lawyer reviews every mark-up and decides what advice is given, and juniors spend more of their time on the analysis they are trained for.

items.question: Which practice management and document systems does it work with?
items.answer: Any matter management, document management or billing system with an API or a reliable export, along with Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace for email and calendars and the public eCourts services for case status. In the first week we confirm what your setup exposes.

items.question: What about client confidentiality and privilege?
items.answer: Documents stay in your own document store or a private environment set up for the firm, and are not used to train any public model. Matter-level permissions and ethical walls apply to every search, and all access is logged. The setup follows the DPDP Act 2023 for personal data, and the GDPR where you act for clients in Europe.

items.question: Can it work with documents in Indian languages?
items.answer: Yes. It can read and search documents and talk to clients in Hindi, Marathi, Tamil and other Indian languages as well as English. For filings and court translations a lawyer or certified translator still checks the text.

items.question: What happens if the AI gets a date or a clause wrong?
items.answer: Dates computed by the agent are shown to a lawyer to confirm, and every contract change is a tracked suggestion, not a final edit. Where it is unsure, it says so. Each correction is fed back so the same mistake is caught next time.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on the number of lawyers, courts and systems involved. Most firms start with hearing-date tracking and intake, which are quick to set up; tell us about your practice and we'll send a fixed quote for that first phase.
